title: I built a tool that explains why price moved. Looking for traders to test it.
author: KimOnMacro
selftext:
I've been building around one simple idea:  
**You can see what price did. But do you know why it moved?**   
  
V3 of my app just dropped, and I’ve rebuilt a lot of the core analysis based on feedback from my current users.  


The biggest changes are:

**A New Fundamental Bias system**  
A clearer way to understand the underlying factors influencing an instrument by using macro values and a deterministic points system  
  
**Much deeper candle-specific analysis**  
Pick a specific candle or move and investigate what was happening around that exact move (headlines as well as macro summary)  
  
**Live Recent Market Context**  
Instead of looking at the chart in isolation, Echelon continuously builds a live picture of what is influencing the asset and keeps it updated as conditions change.  


**I've already gone through feedback with my current users who've tried V1 and V2, but now I want to get some fresh eyes from traders who haven't been using Echelon every day.**  


So I'm giving **1 month free** to anyone who genuinely wants to test it and give me honest feedback.  
Tell me what you like, what you don't, what's confusing, or what you think is missing. (Obviously happy for you to stop using it after the free access if its not your thing)  
  
Just comment if you want to try it or DM me and I'll send you a free month  
I may, however, aggressively request your feedback so I can make V4 better. 😂  
  
[https://echelonedgeai.com/](https://echelonedgeai.com/)

comments.author: KimOnMacro
comments.body: oh also, happy to answer anything about how it works too.

replies.author: KimOnMacro
replies.body:
Yep the idea is pretty simple. You pick an instrument and a specific price move, and Echelon looks at what was happening around that move to help explain why it happened.  
  
It pulls together things like recent market context, economic events, fundamental data, positioning and other relevant information, then connects that back to the specific candle you're investigating.

The main value for me is the context around the price. You can see a huge candle on a chart, but the candle itself doesn't tell you what caused it. There could have been a major economic release, a trump war tweet, a shift in institutional positioning, a headline, or a combination of things happening around the same time.   
  
So rather than just looking at the chart and guessing what happened, Echelon gives you the surrounding context and helps you understand what may have been driving the move.

replies.author: Fire-Engineering
replies.body: If ifs and ands were pots and pans, there'd be no work for tinkers.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: I'd be careful with the candle-level headline match. a headline two minutes before a move gets credit for it whether it caused anything or not, and most big candles have some headline nearby. showing the times it says "no clear catalyst" would do more for trust than any new feature.

replies.author: KimOnMacro
replies.body:
Really appreciate you bringing this up. This is exactly the kind of feedback that’s useful!  
  
I really like this point and I've made sure to frame nearby headlines as potential factors rather than saying they were definitively the cause, but I think making the “no clear catalyst” cases more obvious would add a lot of trust to the analysis. Thank you!

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: "potential factor" is the right wording. a visible "nothing obvious here" on a big candle would honestly make me trust the hits more.

replies.author: KimOnMacro
replies.body: Yep. I guess it'll also give you a useful baseline too, because you can see when the system didnt find anything convincing rather than assuming every big move must have an explanation sitting right next to it. Definitely something I’ll look at adding!

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: a hit rate shown right next to the misses is what I'd check first before trusting any label. curious how often it ends up saying it found nothing.

replies.author: KimOnMacro
replies.body: Yeah, I’m curious about that too. Seeing how often it finds something meaningful versus when there’s genuinely nothing obvious going on would tell me a lot, and could also help me work out how to reduce any noise in the analysis.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: yeah, the no-catalyst rate is probably the best number you have for tuning the noise down. if a change cuts false hits and that rate barely moves, it worked.

replies.author: KimOnMacro
replies.body: Hey, appreciate all your insight and feedback quantradin!

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: anytime. post the no-catalyst numbers once you have a week of them, I'd read that.
